name: Whale
description: Long-range acoustic intelligence navigating ocean basins through song, magnetic sensing, and multi-generational cultural memory.

core_attributes.pattern: long-range acoustic communication, magnetic navigation, cultural transmission

scope.definition: Fraction of original song energy detectable at 1000 km in SOFAR channel, averaged across blue/fin/humpback species under typical North Atlantic conditions.

evidence.source: Payne & McVay (1971) 'Songs of Humpback Whales', Science 173:585-597; Watkins et al. (2000) 'Twentieth-century records of 20-Hz signals', Deep-Sea Research 47:1543-1562.
cross_domain_examples: blue whale 20 Hz calls detectable 1000+ km in SOFAR channel
fin whale 20 Hz pulses: 800 km range verified by hydrophone arrays
humpback song: cross-ocean-basin pattern fidelity 0.96 per Payne (1971)
seismic array detection of whale calls at 3000 km (anomalous propagation)

scope.falsifiability: If whale acoustic transmission efficiency is measured below 0.5 at 1000 km consistently, the SOFAR channel waveguide model fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Efficiency degrades with ocean noise pollution, temperature inversions, and shipping traffic. SOFAR efficiency assumes clean mid-ocean propagation; near shipping lanes values drop to 0.6-0.75.

scope.definition: Probability that a whale stays within 5% of optimal magnetic-field-aligned migratory route per 100 km segment, based on stranding pattern alignment and magnetite tissue studies.

evidence.source: Klinowska (1985) 'Cetacean stranding sites relate to geomagnetic topography', Aquatic Mammals 11:27-32; Zoeger et al. (1981) magnetite in cetacean tissue, Science 213:892-894.
cross_domain_examples: whale stranding sites correlate with geomagnetic minima (Klinowska 1985)
magnetite crystals found in dura mater of 12 cetacean species
satellite-tagged humpbacks follow magnetic isolines during migration

scope.falsifiability: If stranding sites show no correlation with geomagnetic anomalies across a dataset of 500+ strandings, the magnetic navigation hypothesis is unsupported.
scope.measurement_limits: Stranding correlation is statistical, not mechanistic proof. Solar storms disrupt magnetic navigation; anomalous strandings increase during geomagnetic disturbances.

scope.definition: Proportion of novel song motifs (new phrases or sequences) that spread from innovating males to ≥50% of males in the same ocean basin within two breeding seasons.

evidence.source: Noad et al. (2000) 'Cultural revolution in whale songs', Nature 408:537; Garland et al. (2011) 'Dynamic horizontal cultural transmission of humpback whale song', Current Biology 21:687-691.
cross_domain_examples: novel Australian humpback song replaced entire Pacific repertoire within 2 years (Garland 2011)
eastern/western Pacific populations share song themes despite no physical contact
song complexity increases over decades via cumulative cultural layering

scope.falsifiability: If song motifs remain isolated within ocean basins for 10+ years with no cross-population spread, cultural transmission via acoustic contact is not the primary mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Transmission speed depends on population density and acoustic overlap zones. Atlantic-Pacific cultural exchange has not been observed, setting geographic limits.
